role: CHAIN VALIDATOR (HypER-inspired, prompted; not the trained HypER SLM)
distractor_note: Distractors D1/D2 were injected into link 1 of P1-C02, P1-C07, P2-C01, P2-C09. The same model wrote and validated the chains, so this is a NON-BLIND sanity check of the labelling rule, not evidence of validator reliability.
labels: Transitions t1..t5 connect links 1->2 ... 5->6. S=SUPPORTED, W=WEAK, I=INVALID. Links: 1 evidence, 2 limitation, 3 problem, 4 reasoning, 5 mechanism, 6 hypothesis.

links: Single pre-generation probe on 3-hop chains; step triggers exist only for retrieval
No measurement of step-wise vs single-decision headroom for multi-call tool chains
Quantify oracle headroom of step-wise decisions
If necessity depends on intermediate values, a pre-generation decision cannot see it
Counterfactual branching per step, oracle U-AUC comparison
Step-wise oracle exceeds single oracle by >= 2 U-AUC points
chains.first_break: t3 (W): no cited evidence that necessity varies within chains; E7's high multi-hop AUROC suggests it may be predictable upfront.
chains.verdict: KEEP - falsifiable measurement; the weak link is exactly what the experiment tests.

links: Need-probes predict difficulty, not marginal effect of calling
Two heads on h_t can recover p_call and p_nocall
MUP beats step-wise need probe on U-AUC
chains.first_break: t1 (I): D1 concerns biomedical hypothesis evaluation and supports nothing about tool calling. Distractor correctly rejected. After removing D1 (replace with E12, E20), t1 = S. t3 remains W: E12 reports utility estimation is weak at instance level - evidence against easy learnability.
chains.verdict: KEEP with risk flag (E12 is counter-evidence).

links: Regret-weighted, Bayes-aligned stopping beats score thresholds under heterogeneous cost
Subtracting two noisy probabilities amplifies error; decisions need only the sign
Learn the decision sign directly, conditioned on cost
Regret weighting focuses capacity on high-stakes steps
Cost-sensitive scorer g(h_t, lambda*c) trained with sampled lambda
Lower per-step regret than two-head subtraction
chains.first_break: t4 (W): E17 proves alignment for prefix stopping over tool rankings, not call/no-call per reasoning step; transfer is plausible but unproven.
chains.verdict: KEEP.

links: Sequential cost-aware decisions benefit from explicit value reasoning
Optimise trajectory utility with continuation value
Fitted-Q on logged branches can estimate continuation value
FQI beats one-step rules when errors propagate
chains.first_break: t1 (W): no evidence that one-step rules are materially suboptimal in 3-hop chains.
chains.verdict: KEEP for review; high feasibility risk (offline RL on small branched data).

links: Most steps do not change the decision
Halve probe calls without U loss
chains.first_break: t2 (I): E34 shows a linear probe costs < 1 ms per task; the motivating limitation is contradicted by evidence.
chains.verdict: REJECT - premise contradicted (overhead is negligible for linear probes).

links: Conformal risk control calibrates step-level risk in agents
Thresholds give no bound on missed necessary calls
chains.first_break: t3 (I): steps within a trajectory are not exchangeable (dependent hops), so standard split-conformal guarantees do not transfer without trajectory-level calibration; E30 (abstract only) does not establish it for call decisions.
chains.verdict: REVISE (trajectory-level calibration) or REJECT.

links: Single pre-generation probe already strong on 3-hop
Use step-wise probing only where the single probe is uncertain
Uncertain pre-generation predictions mark instances where necessity is revealed later
Cascade matches step-wise U-AUC with fewer evaluations
chains.first_break: t1 (I): D2 is about call format, not necessity; distractor correctly rejected. Replace with E6/E7 -> S.
chains.verdict: KEEP but note: overhead saving is minor given E34; value is in robustness, not speed.

links: Necessity has three causes; estimators use one fixed representation
A tool embedding lets one probe share structure across tools
chains.first_break: t2 (W): E13 is about representation choice, not per-tool training; motivation partly inferred.
chains.verdict: KEEP for review; hypothesis 'above chance' is too weak.

links: Label definition for steps is unexamined
chains.verdict: KEEP but overlaps P1-C01/P1-C02 (label construction); candidate for merge.

links: Test a single cost-conditioned rule out of range
Conditioning on lambda generalises if score is calibrated
chains.verdict: KEEP as ablation, weak standalone novelty.

links: Priors in context change agent behaviour; prefill steers
Actuation mode for step estimates untested
Small non-thinking models follow prefill better than numeric priors
chains.verdict: KEEP as ablation; incremental.

links: Token-probability triggers and hidden-state probes both exist
No comparison for step-level tool utility
Hidden states encode more than output probabilities
chains.first_break: t3 (W): E6 compares against verbalized reasoning, not token probabilities.
chains.verdict: KEEP as ablation.

links: Black-box rule uses a global p_ret
Estimate per-query tool benefit without internals
Query features predict whether the tool will help
chains.first_break: t1 (I): D1 irrelevant - correctly rejected; replace with E14/E15 -> S. t3 (W): E12 suggests utility prediction is hard even white-box.
chains.verdict: KEEP with risk flag.

links: p_ret is global; necessity has execution causes
Preview signals (retrieval scores, parse size) correlate with tool success
Preview features feed p_tool_hat, cost charged
Preview pays for itself on retrieval
chains.verdict: KEEP; scenario-specific (strong for retrieval, trivial for calculator).

links: Consistency needs samples; explicit modelling adds latency
Adapt the number of samples per query
Many queries are decided after 1-2 samples
Fixed-k=10 U-AUC with < 4 samples on average
chains.verdict: KEEP; directly answers G5 (signal overhead).

links: Hidden states encode necessity; counterfactual labels
Predict target's benefit from a proxy's internals
Proxy and target share difficulty structure
chains.first_break: t3 (I): no evidence that a small proxy's representations track a larger model's knowledge boundary; knowledge boundaries are model-specific (E11's need is defined per model).
chains.verdict: REVISE or REJECT.

links: Confidently-wrong cases explain most of the gap
chains.verdict: KEEP; analysis rather than solution.

links: Conformal risk control exists for agents
No guarantee on accuracy loss from skipped calls
chains.first_break: t1 (W): E30 abstract-level.
chains.verdict: KEEP; single-decision setting makes exchangeability plausible (unlike P1-C06).

links: Recalibrate under shift with few labels
Few labels suffice for monotone maps
chains.verdict: KEEP; general calibration result, modest tool-specific novelty.

links: Counterfactual benefit labels; query routers exist
chains.first_break: t3 (W); novelty limited by E35 (query routers exist).
chains.verdict: KEEP as low-cost baseline/variant.

links: Verbalized confidence covers only direct side
Models can estimate tool helpfulness verbally
chains.first_break: t1 (I): distractor correctly rejected. Also t3 (W): E27 says verbalized confidence is overconfident.
chains.verdict: KEEP for review.

chains.first_break: t1 (W): bandit feedback requires knowing correctness online, which is unavailable in deployment without labels - contradicts its own motivation.
chains.verdict: REJECT - online reward needs ground truth it assumes is missing.

links: Execution reliability is a necessity cause; trajectory risk
Decide after the call whether to trust
chains.first_break: t2 (I): P2 is a pre-call decision problem; post-call trust is a different problem (scope drift).
chains.verdict: REJECT for P2 (out of scope); note as future work.

links: Independent model errors are partly uncorrelated
chains.verdict: KEEP for review; costs a second model call.
